name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Any person born outside Tanzania on or after Union Day (26 April 1964) is a citizen by descent if one of their parents -- mother or father, applied equally -- is a citizen of Tanzania by birth or naturalization (Citizenship Act 1995, Section 6).

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Tanzanian citizenship (by birth or naturalization)

sources.title: Embassy of Tanzania, Washington D.C. -- official statement that a person born outside Tanzania on or after Union Day is a citizen by descent if one of their parents (mother or father) is a Tanzanian citizen by birth or naturalization

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Tanzania). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct official-embassy sourcing, tier 1. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: descent citizenship is gender-neutral on its face -- either parent transmits it equally, with no separate or lesser maternal-line provision -- joining Kenya, Pakistan (post-2000), India (post-1992), and Tunisia (post-2010) in this dataset as having a reformed, equal descent rule, in contrast to Iran and Lebanon's paternal-default systems built earlier in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set FALSE with higher confidence than in several other countries' files: the Citizenship Act's Section 7 requires a Tanzanian citizen who also holds another nationality to renounce it, take an oath of allegiance, and make a residence declaration (typically by age 18) or automatically lose Tanzanian citizenship -- Tanzania does not generally permit dual citizenship. This was cross-referenced via a Refworld-hosted (tier 2) copy of the Citizenship Act 1995 in this build, not solely the tier-1 embassy source, but the tier-1 source is what's cited on this specific hard requirement per the 'no tier-1, no publish' rule.
